title: AI Rollback and Incident Closeout
summary: Restore a verified AI workflow, reconcile state and side effects, prove recovery, and close an incident only after corrective work has accountable evidence.
prerequisites: A contained incident with an accountable incident commander
A known verified configuration or safe degraded mode
Operation journals, data migration records, and communication ownership

sections.title: Restore behavior and reconcile state
paragraphs: Choose the smallest approved recovery shape that bounds harm: disable the feature, restore application or prompt configuration, return to a verified model or provider route, rebuild a corrupted index, fail over, or use a manual process. Confirm compatibility before rollback; code, prompts, schemas, data, indexes, policies, tools, and records may have changed together.

Changing traffic does not reverse completed or uncertain side effects. Use operation identifiers, journals, idempotency evidence, data checks, compensating actions, and human review queues to classify every consequential operation as confirmed correct, corrected, cancelled, duplicated and repaired, or still unresolved.

sections.title: Prove recovery before closing
paragraphs: Verify the restored user journey, quality and safety gates, permissions, tool postconditions, data integrity, latency, capacity, cost, alerts, support readiness, and communications. Keep heightened monitoring for a declared window. Write a blameless timeline and contributing factors, add the minimized failure to the regression set, assign corrective and preventive work, rehearse the changed runbook, and document residual risk.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the authorized rollback target, deployed-version proof, recovery timing, reconciled operation journal, integrity checks, passing quality and safety gates, monitoring observations, communications, root-cause record, regression case, tracked follow-up work, residual-risk acceptance, and closeout approvals. Verify from the user boundary through provider, tools, data, and external postconditions.

Do not close when any blocking gate fails, a consequential side effect remains unresolved without an accepted owner, the incident recurs during observation, affected users or authorities still require communication, corrective work is untracked, or residual risk lacks acceptance. Recovery from a failed rollback means re-containing the workflow, using another preapproved verified path or manual process, preserving evidence, and reopening the decision log.
sections.callout: Rollback restores software behavior; reconciliation restores trustworthy state.

sections.title: Scenario A continuation: simulation boundary, bounded scope, and authority
paragraphs: Simulation boundary: This is a fictional offline tabletop continuation of IR-FAKE-20260920-001. Every person, identifier, authority, artifact, timestamp, observation, decision, and result below is an exercise fixture. Nothing represents live execution, production evidence, an actual approval, a legal conclusion, a notification, external communication, or successful production recovery. The preserved starting snapshot is 2026-09-20T10:40:00Z: containment VERIFIED, recovery NOT_AUTHORIZED, op-fake-90217 UNRESOLVED, and scope enumeration PENDING.

At 10:52:00Z, Samir Okafor completed a read-only query of the fictional authoritative admission journal for route /internal/document-assistant, edges edge-a through edge-c, workers w1 through w6, and the closed interval 10:01:48.221Z through 10:07:40.000Z. The terminal watermark was admission_seq=88421. The query returned exactly three parent execution requests and no additional parent execution request through that watermark. These counts are bounded by the stated route, infrastructure, interval, and watermark. The upper scope outside that boundary is UNKNOWN.

The journal term parent_request means an admitted execution envelope, not necessarily an independent user submission. Two parent execution requests, req-fake-4401 and req-fake-4402, were generated from the same actual user submission user-request-fake-1842-01 and share trace-fake-7c91. The first admitted retrieval operation op-fake-90216. The second was an internal continuation envelope that admitted update operation op-fake-90217. The third parent execution request, req-fake-4403, came from a separate actual user submission user-request-fake-1842-02, used trace-fake-7c92, and admitted retrieve operation op-fake-90218.

The resulting bounded cardinalities are therefore two actual user submissions, three admitted parent execution envelopes, two traces, three tool operations, one user identity, and two document identities. Merely listing three parent identifiers would not establish these distinct counts. The mapping records both the originating user-request ID and the admitted parent execution ID so an auditor can reproduce each cardinality. The supplied exercise records do not establish whether the named staging lane, fixture stores, or actors correspond to any real system or production store.

At 11:02:00Z, Luis Ortega obtained terminal evidence for op-fake-90217. The worker lease service returned cancel-ack-fake-90217 with fence 7714. Document version history remained v41, audit mutation rows were zero, the idempotency commit was absent, worker commit rows were zero, retry rows were zero, and no lease remained capable of committing after the fence. This resolves the earlier UNKNOWN state as CANCELLED without replay, reversal, or compensation.

The authorized isolated staging/test lane is a fictional, offline exercise harness consisting only of the candidate artifact set named in auth-fake-004, the synthetic document doc-test-recovery-001, its independent staging version store, its test index identity index-fixture-882, and synthetic request fixtures. The candidate artifact set is app doc-assist-2026.09.20.3, config cfg-authz-2026.09.20.3, prompt prompt-doc-edit-2026.09.20.3, model model-ref-fictitious-7, retrieve_document@tool-retrieve-v4, update_document@tool-update-v5, policy P42-AUTHZ-2026.09.20.3, schema document-action-v3, and index doc-index-2026.09.20.2. Authorized lane actors are Elena Rossi for preparation and deployment actions, Samir Okafor for independent readback and tests, Luis Ortega for operation reconciliation, Priya Shah for restricted evidence access, and Maya Chen for the later decision. These actor assignments are exercise records, not independently established production roles.

The staging lane has no production-state bypass. Its writes are limited to doc-test-recovery-001 in the independent staging store. It may not read or mutate doc-fin-311, may not use production durable state as a test fixture, may not replay op-fake-90217, and may not restore route admission or enable production update behavior. Positive tests at 11:24:00Z therefore run through the isolated lane while all production edges remain paused and production update_document remains disabled until 11:38:00Z. The staging proof is pre-restoration evidence about the candidate behavior, not evidence that the live service has recovered. Later post-restoration monitoring begins only with the 11:39:00Z independent readback.

Authority was separated by purpose. Preparation authority auth-fake-003, issued at 11:08:00Z, permitted read-only scope, compatibility work, synthetic tests, and fixture-only preparation in the isolated lane. It specifically covered doc-test-recovery-001 in the independent staging store, including the authorized v7-to-v8 idempotent test, but permitted no deployment, re-enablement, replay, reversal, or mutation of doc-fin-311. Deploy authority auth-fake-004, issued at 11:16:00Z, named the exact target, route, edges, workers, and fixture-only writes. It allowed deployment and readback but required a later accountable decision before re-enablement. Both records are fictional and expire at the stated times. The dossier does not provide a first-party source establishing a real staging/test-lane definition, real actors, or separation from production stores, so those boundaries are exercise assumptions rather than external facts.

sections.title: Scenario A: compatible recovery shape, rejected rollback, and fallback
paragraphs: The selected recovery shape was controlled forward restoration. It changed the application, prompt, configuration, and authorization policy while retaining the verified model reference, tool contracts, schema, durable document data, and index. This was the smallest reviewed shape that added the missing document-workspace predicate without introducing a schema or index migration. Restoration of behavior and reconciliation of durable state remained separate decisions.

The old set was app doc-assist-2026.09.20.2, prompt prompt-doc-edit-2026.09.20.2, model model-ref-fictitious-7, tools retrieve_document@tool-retrieve-v4 and update_document@tool-update-v5, policy P42-AUTHZ-2026.09.20.2, schema document-action-v3, and index doc-index-2026.09.20.2. The new set changed the app, prompt, configuration, and policy suffix to .3 while retaining the model, tools, schema, and index. Opaque fixture IDs identify exercise artifacts. They are not cryptographic hashes.

The isolated compatibility lane used staging-store-fake-01 and doc-test-recovery-001. Its initial staging version was v7. The production document doc-fin-311 remained in the separate bounded exercise record at v41. The supplied dossier does not independently establish that these stores represent real staging and production systems, so the separation is an explicit tabletop fixture boundary, not a production claim.

Compatibility was established through six reproducible cases. COMP-01 compared the old and new retrieve input fields. COMP-02 compared update input fields and the external_commit_status output. COMP-03 validated four literal normalized response fixtures against the compact minimum document-action-v3 shape. COMP-04 compared the deployed index identity with the target manifest. COMP-05 checked the migration plan for data, schema, and index changes. COMP-06 ran retrieval and an idempotent update against the synthetic staging fixture and read back its durable staging version. Every observed result matched its recorded expectation.

For COMP-01, the compared external keys were user_id, request_workspace, and document_id. The new policy also used document_workspace and role as internal policy context derived by the service, but those are not external request keys and were not accepted as caller-supplied authorization evidence. The comparison therefore found zero missing required external fields and zero extra external fields. The internal policy context comparison is recorded separately because treating it as external input would weaken the boundary being tested.

The compact minimum response shape for document-action-v3 requires an object with operation_id, status, document_id, and result. status must be exactly one of COMPLETED, COMMITTED, DENIED, CANCELLED, or UNKNOWN. operation_id, status, and document_id are required strings. result is required as an object and must contain only the bounded result fields appropriate to the status. A COMPLETED retrieval includes title and version in result. A COMMITTED update includes version and external_commit_status=COMMITTED in result. A DENIED response includes reason_code and retrieval_performed=false. A CANCELLED response includes cancellation_reason and mutation_committed=false. No response may claim a successful user-visible mutation unless the corresponding status is COMMITTED and the authoritative readback agrees.

COMP-06 occurred at 11:14:00Z, before deploy authority auth-fake-004 was issued at 11:16:00Z. It was authorized by auth-fake-003, used the independent staging store, started at doc-test-recovery-001:v7, committed once with idempotency key idem-test-001 to v8, and repeated the same key without creating a second commit. This preparation result did not deploy anything and did not write doc-fin-311. The later 11:24:00Z positive tests reused the same isolated lane and verified the already recorded v7-to-v8 state without bypassing paused production edges or disabled production update behavior.

The older rollback target doc-assist-2026.09.20.1 with cfg-authz-2026.09.20.1 was deliberately rejected and never deployed. Its update response lacked external_commit_status, its declared schema was document-action-v2, its index reference was index-fixture-771 rather than index-fixture-882, and its test inventory lacked a mismatched-document-workspace case. A command response claiming success could not substitute for these incompatible readbacks.

The safe fallback remained active while compatibility and deployment were evaluated: admission stayed paused, update_document stayed disabled, retries stayed frozen, and permitted work used manual review. A fixture request at 11:14:00Z returned MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED, with retrieval and mutation both not performed.

sections.title: Scenario A: exact recovery procedure and complete consequential-operation journal
paragraphs: 1. At 11:16:00Z, Elena Rossi recorded rb-fake-007 before deployment. All three edges were paused, update_document was disabled on all six workers, retries were frozen, and the old artifact set remained deployed. Auth-fake-004 was valid and unexpired.

2. At 11:20:00Z, Elena deployed only the target named in auth-fake-004. The deployment response was not treated as proof. Samir Okafor independently read back every application, configuration, prompt, model, tool, policy, schema, and index identifier at 11:21:00Z.

3. At 11:24:00Z, Samir ran the authorization, safety, user-journey, quality, tool, data, index, latency, and capacity cases recorded in the gate section. Synthetic mutations were limited to doc-test-recovery-001. No test wrote doc-fin-311.

4. At 11:28:00Z, Luis reconciled all three consequential operations returned by scope-fake-004. Op-fake-90216 was classified CONFIRMED_UNAUTHORIZED_DISCLOSURE because a foreign restricted title was returned. Op-fake-90217 was classified CANCELLED using terminal lease fencing and durable readbacks. Op-fake-90218 was classified CONFIRMED_CORRECT because its request and document workspaces matched and it produced no mutation. No operation remained unresolved, no unknown operation was replayed, and no compensation was required.

5. At 11:31:00Z, Priya Shah completed the blocking privacy and evidence-access review through the fictional restricted path. Document doc-fin-311 remained v41, with the same opaque fixture identifier before and after. Index identity remained index-fixture-882. Cache and export metadata queries returned zero rows for the bounded requests.

6. At 11:34:00Z, Maya Chen issued decision-fake-010 authorizing controlled re-enablement after reviewing the pre-reenable gate ledger. At 11:38:00Z, Elena restored route admission and update_document on the named infrastructure. This timestamp marks service restoration, not verified sustained recovery.

7. At 11:39:00Z, Samir independently confirmed enabled route and worker state plus the target artifact set. This was the initial post-restoration state readback and the start of monitoring. Sustained recovery was not declared verified until the observation window ended at 12:39:00Z.

8. The monitored window ran from 11:39:00Z through 12:39:00Z, exactly 60 minutes. Six ten-minute checkpoints showed no authorization mismatch alert, restricted disclosure, unexpected write, retry of op-fake-90217, artifact drift, or failed negative test. Final sustained-recovery verification occurred at 12:39:00Z.

Elapsed arithmetic is explicit: detection at 10:02:11Z to containment verification at 10:08:15Z equals 6 minutes 4 seconds. Deployment start at 11:20:00Z to service restoration at 11:38:00Z equals 18 minutes. Restoration at 11:38:00Z to initial independent readback at 11:39:00Z equals 1 minute. Initial readback at 11:39:00Z to sustained-recovery verification at 12:39:00Z equals 60 minutes. Detection at 10:02:11Z to sustained-recovery verification at 12:39:00Z equals 2 hours 36 minutes 49 seconds.

sections.title: Scenario A: reproducible pre-reenable gates, isolated user journeys, and observations
paragraphs: Maya Chen fixed the fictional local thresholds at 11:15:00Z, before gate execution. These thresholds are exercise criteria, not laws, standards, or general production recommendations. Re-enablement required every permission, safety, user-journey, quality, tool, data, index, latency, and capacity case to pass, zero cross-workspace allows, zero unauthorized fixture mutations, p95 latency no greater than 1000 milliseconds, all six workers healthy, and aggregate queue depth no greater than 2.

At 11:24:00Z, production admission remained paused on edge-a through edge-c and production update_document remained disabled on workers w1 through w6. The positive user-journey cases ran only in the authorized isolated staging/test lane defined in auth-fake-003 and auth-fake-004. The candidate artifact set was tested against doc-test-recovery-001 in staging-store-fake-01. The lane did not bypass production state, did not read or mutate doc-fin-311, and did not constitute live service recovery.

The permission set used six cases. AUTH-01 and AUTH-02 tested permitted retrieval and update in ws-redwood-internal. AUTH-03 tested a disallowed role in a matching workspace. AUTH-04 and AUTH-05 tested cross-workspace retrieval and update. AUTH-06 combined a cross-workspace document with a disallowed role. Inputs, expected decisions, observed decisions, and postconditions are included below. All six matched expectations, and every reject occurred before retrieval or mutation.

The user-journey cases traced each synthetic user request through policy evaluation, tool response, authoritative readback, and the bounded user-visible result. UJ-01 allowed retrieval of doc-hr-017 and returned only its synthetic title and version after a retrieval readback. UJ-02 allowed one idempotent update of doc-test-recovery-001 in the staging lane, returned COMMITTED only after the v7-to-v8 readback, and returned no additional commit on the repeated idempotency key. UJ-03 blocked cross-workspace retrieval of doc-fin-311 before the tool, returned DENIED to the synthetic user, and excluded title and body. UJ-04 blocked an attempted update of doc-fin-311 before mutation, returned DENIED, and excluded restricted content and any success claim. Expected and observed results matched all four cases.

The safety set used four restricted-document cases. SAFE-01 tested title retrieval, SAFE-02 tested body retrieval, SAFE-03 tested update, and SAFE-04 tested an instruction asking the assistant to ignore workspace policy. All expected and observed REJECT. Independent tool, version, and response readbacks showed zero restricted titles, zero bodies, zero mutations, and no unsupported success message.

Quality cases checked four response shapes rather than recording labels alone. Q-01 was an allowed retrieval response, Q-02 an allowed update response, Q-03 a denied retrieval response, and Q-04 a cancelled operation response. All conformed to the compact document-action-v3 requirements and used the required status. Tool cases TOOL-01 through TOOL-04 paired each tool result with a distinct authoritative postcondition readback. No assistant message was accepted by itself.

Data and index checks compared exact before and after observations. Doc-fin-311 remained v41 and doc-test-recovery-001 changed only during its authorized fixture update from staging v7 to staging v8. Index identity remained index-fixture-882. Twenty latency samples all fell below 1000 milliseconds; sorted sample 19 of 20, used as the nearest-rank p95, was 712 milliseconds.

Capacity was measured before the 11:34:00Z re-enablement decision, not during the later monitoring window. Six observations from 11:25:00Z through 11:30:00Z each found all six workers healthy. Aggregate queue depths were 0, 1, 0, 2, 1, and 0, each at or below the immutable threshold of 2. These pre-restoration staging proofs did not establish sustained live recovery. The later post-restoration monitoring window began with the 11:39:00Z independent readback.

sections.title: Scenario A: post-recovery gates, root cause, residual risk, and fictional closeout
paragraphs: The 60-minute post-restoration window retained the predeclared zero-tolerance thresholds for authorization mismatch alerts, restricted disclosures, unexpected writes, and retries of op-fake-90217. Six checkpoints passed. Cost used six consecutive ten-minute windows with an immutable threshold of no more than 15 fictional cost units per window. The observations 14, 11, 13, 12, 9, and 7 sum to 66 units. This is an exercise metric, not a production cost estimate.

Support readiness used two exact observations. SUP-01 retrieved the on-call procedure containing the re-contain, evidence-preservation, and terminal-fence steps. SUP-02 retrieved the manual-review fallback containing the no-retrieval and no-mutation conditions. The fictional communications decision was recorded at 12:42:00Z by Maya Chen after consultation with Priya Shah and Jordan Lee. It authorized no external contact and asserted no real legal, regulatory, contractual, or notification conclusion.

Root-cause confidence is MEDIUM. Configuration evidence shows the affected retrieval filter compared user workspace with request workspace but omitted document workspace, and the minimized corrected case rejects the same cross-workspace input. Alternative implementation or propagation defects were not completely eliminated. The supported statement is therefore likely authorization-predicate omission within the reviewed configuration, not a proven universal cause.

Regression case REG-AUTHZ-003 uses user workspace ws-redwood-internal, document workspace ws-birch-internal, role policy-editor, and both retrieve_document and update_document. Expected postconditions are rejection before retrieval or mutation, no title or body, no audit mutation, unchanged version v41, and no success claim. The old fixture allowed retrieval; the restored fixture rejected both variants with the expected readbacks.

All blocking conditions were evaluated only after sustained-recovery verification at 12:39:00Z. Scope enumeration was complete, all three operations had terminal classifications, no consequential effect remained unresolved, compatibility and pre-reenable gates passed, the target set was independently read back, the monitored window completed without recurrence, required privacy review was complete, support and communications decisions were recorded, owners existed, and residual risk was accepted within the fictional exercise.

Preventive follow-ups remain open with accountable owners and due dates. They are nonblocking because they address future hardening rather than missing evidence needed for the bounded closeout. The preventive privacy review might discover evidence that changes the current assessment. Closure therefore rests only on the evidence available through 12:55:00Z and must reopen if that review finds an additional affected request, user, document, disclosure, mutation, unauthorized evidence access, policy-required communication, or contradiction in terminal state.

Maya Chen accepted a MEDIUM residual risk at 12:50:00Z: effects outside the enumerated route, infrastructure, identities, documents, and time boundary were not ruled out by this exercise. At 12:55:00Z, Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Priya Shah, and Elena Rossi recorded fictional tabletop closeout. This is not a production approval.

Trace-fake-c704 is a separate observed delayed-worker trace with an explicit trace_id field, linked to the same parent req-fake-c8001 and the same operation op-fake-88001. It must be counted as a second trace, not inferred to be merely a span.

Specific feedback: Op-fake-88000 confirms at least one unauthorized restricted-title disclosure. Op-fake-88001 remains UNRESOLVED because success text, the delayed trace, timed-out authoritative services, and UNKNOWN idempotency do not establish whether an annotation committed. The delayed trace confirms another observed trace record for the same operation, but it does not establish a second operation, a second user submission, or a durable commit.

Containment feedback: Admission is verified paused on edge-f and edge-g. Annotation is verified disabled on w12 through w15. Retrieval is verified disabled only on w12 and w13 and remains enabled on w14 and w15. Full containment therefore fails. The 09:15:00Z mismatch alert on w14 is a recurrence signal and an immediate blocking condition.

Authority feedback: Auth-fake-c701 already names w14 and w15, authorizes disable_retrieve, remains unexpired, and contains no one-attempt limit. Under the supplied fictional policy facts, Elena may retry that same disable action without a new authority. She must first verify the authority ID, target, constraints, and expiry. An amendment is required only if the action changes, the target expands, a prohibited mutation becomes necessary, or the authority expires. Teaching that every failed first attempt automatically requires new authority would contradict this fixture.

The completed next procedure is: Elena retries disable_retrieve only on w14 and w15 under auth-fake-c701; Samir independently reads back retrieve and annotate state on all four workers; Samir runs synthetic requests that must reject before retrieval and annotation; Luis repeats document-version, audit, idempotency, worker-commit, retry, and lease queries through the approved read-only path; Priya controls sensitive evidence access; Maya reassesses severity and recovery only after those results. Op-fake-88001 must not be replayed or reversed.

The safe fallback is to keep both edges paused, keep both tools disabled wherever verified, freeze retries, preserve trace-fake-c701, trace-fake-c704, and the alert, and route permitted work to manual review without retrieving or annotating doc-med-204. Recovery remains NOT_AUTHORIZED. Closure fails because full containment is unverified, recurrence occurred, a consequential side effect is unresolved, and authoritative state is unavailable.

Owners and cadence are completed rather than merely requested. Maya Chen owns command, severity, and the recovery decision. Elena Rossi owns the in-scope control retry by 09:18:00Z. Samir Okafor owns independent readback by 09:19:00Z and worker-scope investigation. Luis Ortega owns operation reconciliation with retries every five minutes while authoritative services are unavailable. Priya Shah owns privacy-safe evidence access and policy routing. Jordan Lee owns preparation of communications options but may not contact anyone without a decision. Updates occur every five minutes, with the next command checkpoint at 09:20:00Z, and immediately on another alert, a discovered commit, expanding scope, loss of observability, or authority expiry.

Causal key: Supported hypotheses are worker-specific control propagation failure, incorrect worker targeting by the control implementation, and an authorization defect active on w14. The records do not select among them. Root cause remains UNKNOWN. Ownership does not resolve the uncertain annotation, and retrying the control does not reconcile durable state.

NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 provides general incident-response context across preparation, detection, response, and recovery: https://www.nist.gov/publications/incident-response-recommendations-and-considerations-cybersecurity-risk-management-csf. The voluntary NIST AI Risk Management Framework supports governed AI risk management: https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework. These sources do not establish the fictional authority, thresholds, records, decisions, or legal duties.
